project: TutorA Phase 3 Step 3a - SEO Content Clustering (103 live /subjects/[slug] pages)
business_context: TutorA is a 1:1 tutoring marketplace (find-a-vetted-tutor), not a self-paced course platform. Every /subjects/[slug] page was previously a client-side-only modal with ~30 words of content; a technical SEO audit made them real indexable pages. This research question is NOT whether to add grade/curriculum modifiers (already done -- the 103 subjects are already grade/curriculum-differentiated) but whether real SERP evidence supports each already-split entry actually deserving distinct content.
reference_doc: docs/seo-audit-tutora/phase3-clustering/cluster-plan.md (Step 3a for the 53 /courses/[slug] pages -- methodology precedent; page-type mismatch and domain-overlap-tiebreak findings from that doc are cross-checked, not repeated, at the subject level below)

methodology.tiebreak_rule: Scores in the 2-4 range and cases with 0-1 exact-URL overlap but 4+ shared provider domains on different subpages are resolved via domain-overlap tiebreak per skill methodology: same domains, different dedicated subpages = the provider itself already differentiates the content, which is evidence AGAINST merging (unlike the Course-level Test Prep finding, where domain overlap argued FOR merging modifiers of the SAME subject). At the Subject level the recurring pattern is the opposite: major platforms (TutorChase, MyTutor, Wyzant, Varsity Tutors, Tutor.com, Preply) almost always build a dedicated subpage per curriculum/grade-band, which is itself real-world evidence supporting the existing splits.
search_queries_run: Cambridge English exam tutor FCE CAE

subject_course_cross_links_validation.summary: 13 of 25 pairs (all 9 GCSE/IGCSE pairs) show a consistent pattern: the subject-specific query has its OWN fully dedicated SERP ecosystem, distinct from the generic curriculum-level course query. This does NOT mean the cross-link is wrong (parent-curriculum context genuinely helps users), but it does mean these 9 subject pages should NOT be treated as thin spokes of the course page -- each deserves full primary-keyword ownership (title/H1/meta) on its own subject page, with the course cross-link as a secondary 'part of our full GCSE/IGCSE coverage' link, not the other way around. 6 programming-language pairs (javascript, python, c, sql, java, html) confirm the cross-link is directionally correct but flag that the CONTENT TEMPLATE should be practical-mentor-marketplace style, not the credentialed-exam-tutor style used elsewhere. 1 pair (ai-basics) is flagged as a keyword-targeting problem independent of the cross-link. python-basics/python sharing one course is flagged as an audience-differentiation risk worth a follow-up decision.

curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: CONFIRMED -- holds at the granular subject level. Every AP subject searched (Physics 1, Physics C, Physics, Calculus AB, Calculus BC, Calculus, Chemistry, Biology) returns credentialed-tutor-bio / expert-matching pages as the dominant result type (Tutor.com, Wyzant, Princeton Review, Varsity Tutors, AJTutoring, Learner, UPchieve) -- never thin generic product-listing pages. This directly extends the Course-level SXO finding down to the individual AP exam level.
sibling_differentiation: AP Physics 1 vs AP Physics C: WELL DIFFERENTIATED. Zero exact-URL overlap; AP Physics C (calculus-based, split into Mechanics/E&M) has fully dedicated subpages across every provider (Wyzant AP_Physics_C, LA Tutors 123, Growing Stars, TeacherOn, Princeton Review /ap-physics-c, Varsity Tutors, Stemly). Keep separate.

AP Physics 1 vs AP Physics (generic): MODERATE CANNIBALIZATION RISK. 3 of ~7 results are IDENTICAL exact URLs between the two queries (Wyzant AP_physics_tutors.aspx, Princeton Review's tutor-search?s=ap+physics+1 literally serves the generic query too, Jaya's Academy). Since College Board discontinued the old undifferentiated 'AP Physics' exam in 2014 (replaced by Physics 1/2/C), a bare 'AP Physics' subject is somewhat anachronistic. RECOMMEND: reposition the ap-physics subject page as a chooser/overview ('AP Physics 1 vs AP Physics C: which is right for you?') that routes to ap-physics-1 and ap-physics-c, rather than competing head-on with ap-physics-1 for the same primary keyword.

AP Calculus AB vs AP Calculus BC: MODERATE OVERLAP but distinct products. 2 of 6 results are the SAME exact URL for both queries (Learner.com/math-tutoring/ap-calculus, AlexanderTutoring.com/tutoring-resource-guide/ap-calculus-tutors -- both providers explicitly serve AB+BC on one page). Tutor.com and Growing Stars still maintain separate AB/BC subpages. Keep both subject pages but cross-link heavily (siblings, not competitors) since BC content is a superset of AB.

AP Calculus AB vs AP Calculus (generic): CANNIBALIZATION RISK CONFIRMED. Tutor.com's AB-specific URL (tutor.com/subjects/ap-calculus-ab) appears verbatim in the GENERIC 'AP Calculus tutor' SERP -- Google is already treating the AB page as the answer to the generic query. RECOMMEND: reposition ap-calculus (generic) similarly to ap-physics above -- as an AB/BC chooser/overview page, not a third competing primary target.
AP Chemistry, AP Biology: standalone, no sibling subject exists in the catalog, no cannibalization risk found.

curriculum_family_findings.family: GCSE / IGCSE / A-Level Chemistry, Physics, Maths trio
curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: CONFIRMED -- credentialed/DBS-checked-tutor-bio pattern holds (TutorChase, MyTutor, Study Mind, PMT Education, Keystone Tutors, Sherpa all lead with tutor credentials, exam-board coverage, and trust signals, never thin listings).
sibling_differentiation: GCSE Chemistry vs IGCSE Chemistry vs A-Level Chemistry: STRONGLY DIFFERENTIATED. Near-zero domain overlap between any pair (only TutorChase appears across all three, always on a dedicated /gcse/, /igcse/, /a-level/ subpage -- 0 exact URL overlap in any pairing). This is the single cleanest confirmation in the whole research set that the existing 3-way curriculum split is SERP-justified, not over-splitting.
GCSE Physics vs IGCSE Physics vs A-Level Physics: same pattern -- TutorChase and PMT Education maintain separate dedicated subpages for all three curricula; zero exact-URL overlap.

GCSE Maths vs IGCSE Maths: ZERO domain overlap at all (completely different provider sets: Sherpa/Superprof/TheGCSEMathsTutor/PMT for GCSE vs GoStudent/TutorsPlus/igcsemathstutors.com for IGCSE). Fully differentiated.

A-Level Maths vs A-Level Further Maths: MINOR overlap only -- one individual tutor site (alevelmathsrevision.com, John Armstrong) explicitly serves both on one page ('specialist A Level Maths Tutor and A Level Further Maths Tutor'), but every major platform (TutorChase, MyTutor, Tutorful, PMT, Study Mind, GoStudent) maintains separate dedicated subpages. Keep separate, light cross-link as siblings.

GCSE Biology vs GCSE Science (combined) vs GCSE Chemistry/Physics/Maths: all mutually differentiated via dedicated subpages, confirming a true 6-way GCSE subject split (Bio, Chem, Physics, Science-combined, Maths, English) is SERP-supported.

curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: CONFIRMED -- IB Physics and IB Chemistry results lead with 'IB examiner' / 'IB teacher' credential framing (TutorsPlus, Enhanced Prep, ibtutor.us, Varsity Tutors); IB Math results lead with specialist AA/AI-HL/SL credential framing (mathforib.com, IB Math Master, The IB Math Tutor). Credentialed-bio pattern holds.
sibling_differentiation: IB Math vs IB Physics/Chemistry: FULLY SEPARATE provider ecosystems -- IB Math uses specialist math-only sites (Learner, mathforib.com, IB Math Master, The IB Math Tutor) with zero overlap against the Physics/Chemistry provider set. Strongest possible confirmation IB Math deserves its own distinct hub.

IB Physics vs IB Chemistry: HIGH domain overlap (5 shared domains: AmazingTalker, TutorsPlus, Enhanced Prep, Varsity Tutors, ibtutor.us) but ZERO exact-URL overlap -- every one of those 5 providers has a dedicated /physics vs /chemistry subpage. Per the domain-overlap tiebreak, recommend treating IB Physics and IB Chemistry as a linked 'IB Sciences' pair (cross-link to each other, similar to the GCSE <-> GCSE English precedent in the course-level doc) while keeping them as separate primary pages.

international-baccalaureate-ib (general/Diploma) vs the 3 specific subjects: DISTINCT broad-brand provider set (IB Wave, TopIBTutors, Lanterna, ++tutors, Edunade) legitimately serves as the umbrella/pillar page linking to IB Math/Physics/Chemistry as spokes.

curriculum_family_findings.family: SAT / ACT (3 subjects: SAT Math, SAT English, ACT Math)
curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: PARTIALLY DIFFERENT from the course-level 'SAT tutor' / 'ACT tutor' pattern. The course-level doc found Kaplan/Princeton Review/Manhattan Review dominance with score-guarantee trust signals. At the granular Math/English-section level, the dominant providers are MATH-TUTORING SPECIALISTS (Learner.com, Wyzant, Mathnasium) and ENGLISH/WRITING SPECIALISTS (Preply, AJTutoring, PrepScholar, Schoolhouse) rather than the general test-prep brands. This is a genuinely different competitive set from the parent SAT/ACT course pages.
sibling_differentiation: SAT Math vs SAT English: WELL DIFFERENTIATED -- near-zero overlap (only Learner.com shared, on distinct /sat-math vs /sat-english subpages). Keep separate.

SAT Math vs ACT Math: ONE exact-URL match found (mathnasium.com/math-test-preparation serves both queries verbatim) plus Learner.com and Wyzant domain overlap on distinct subpages. Real but partial overlap -- recommend cross-linking SAT Math and ACT Math to each other as 'standardized test math' siblings, but keep as separate pages since the majority of results still differentiate.

SAT Math / SAT English are NOT currently cross-linked to the SAT course page in lib/subject-course-links.ts. Given the distinct provider ecosystem found, recommend a light cross-link (parent-course context) rather than a full merge -- these subjects have earned independent SERP standing.

curriculum_family_findings.family: Cambridge / IELTS English-proficiency exams (Cambridge English, plus IELTS which sits in a separate 'IELTS' curriculum bucket)
curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: CRITICAL KEYWORD-AMBIGUITY FINDING, distinct from every other exam family researched. A plain 'Cambridge English tutor' search returns GEOGRAPHIC results (English tutors located IN the city of Cambridge, MA/UK -- Wyzant Cambridge_MA_English_tutors, Care.com Cambridge MA, Tutors.com Cambridge MA) with ZERO results about the actual Cambridge Assessment English exam suite (FCE/CAE/CPE/PET). Only a more specific query ('Cambridge English exam tutor FCE CAE') surfaces the real exam-prep competitors (Strommen Inc, Preply's dedicated Cambridge-ESOL-FCE-CAE-CPE listing, ExamEnglish.com).
sibling_differentiation: RECOMMEND: retarget the on-page H1/title/meta for the cambridge-english subject away from bare 'Cambridge English tutor' toward 'Cambridge English exam tutor (FCE/CAE/CPE)' or similar exam-code-specific phrasing to avoid Google interpreting the query as location-based. This is a naming/targeting fix, not a page-existence question -- the exam-prep SERP category clearly exists once the keyword is specific enough.

Cambridge English and IELTS both serve overseas English-certification-seekers but are legitimately different exam bodies/formats (Cambridge English certificates never expire; IELTS scores expire after 2 years and serve immigration/university-admission use cases IELTS doesn't share with FCE/CAE). Recommend a light cross-link between the two as sibling 'English proficiency exam' pages rather than a merge.

curriculum_family_findings.family: Programming/Technology (Python, Python Basics, JavaScript, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, AI Basics, Computer Science, Scratch Programming -- 10 subjects, 8 of which are course-cross-linked)
curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: DOES NOT MATCH the credentialed-exam-tutor pattern found everywhere else. Narrow, language-specific queries (Python, JavaScript, Java, C++, SQL, HTML) return a MIX of free self-serve tutorial sites (W3Schools, docs.python.org, learnpython.org, TutorialsPoint, sqltutorial.org) and freelance-mentor marketplaces (Codementor, Preply, Superprof, Upwork) -- a 'practical project mentor' template, not a '99th-percentile examiner with a score guarantee' trust template. The broader 'Computer Science' query, by contrast, DOES match the credentialed-marketplace pattern (Wyzant, Princeton Review, Varsity Tutors, tutor.com, 24HourAnswers) -- breadth of query changes the competitive set within this same category.
sibling_differentiation: Python vs Python Basics: CONFIRMED distinct SERP ecosystems. General 'Python tutor' surfaces adult/general programming resources (learnpython.org, Codementor, pythontutor.net); 'Python basics tutor for kids' surfaces a kids-coding-camp-specific ecosystem (iD Tech, Tynker, CodeWizardsHQ, TeachYourKidsCode) with almost no overlap. The existing grade-band split (Grades 6-8 vs Grades 9-12) IS SERP-justified. See subject_course_cross_links_validation for the audience-split risk this creates against their SHARED course target.

Scratch Programming: fully distinct kids-coding-camp ecosystem (CodaKid, iD Tech, theCoderSchool, Breakout Mentors, Create & Learn), zero overlap with adult languages. Standalone, well-differentiated.
AI Basics: see the flag-keyword-mismatch entry in subject_course_cross_links_validation -- essentially no established tutor-marketplace SERP category for this exact phrasing yet.

curriculum_family_findings.family: Languages (Spanish, French, Hindi, Arabic, Spoken English, plus Cambridge English / IELTS as exam-specific English)
curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: CONFIRMED consistent language-marketplace pattern across every language searched: Preply, italki, Wyzant, Superprof, and AmazingTalker dominate ALL of Spanish, French, Hindi, and Arabic on dedicated per-language subpages (5 shared domains, but 0 exact-URL overlap in every pairing -- the domain-overlap tiebreak here supports keeping each language as its own primary target, matching the pattern already used at the course level for these same 4 languages).
sibling_differentiation: Spoken English is a genuinely distinct intent cluster (Cambly, Loora AI-conversation-practice, AmazingTalker's dedicated /speaking subpage) vs generic written/academic English -- confirms its separate positioning and existing course cross-link.
Arabic surfaces a real content differentiator not present in the other 3 languages (Qur'an recitation / Tajweed / Islamic Studies tutors) worth a dedicated FAQ/section.

curriculum_family_findings.family: Singapore curriculum (PSLE Maths, PSLE Science, O-Level Physics, O-Level Chemistry, O-Level Maths)
curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: CONFIRMED fully distinct, geography-specific ecosystem for every subject searched (SmileTutor, ClubMath.sg, Mavis Tutorial Centre, NickleBee Tutors, TheChemistryPractice.sg, ZenithEducationStudio) -- zero overlap with UK/US tutoring brands seen everywhere else in this research. Singapore subjects should carry Singapore-specific trust signals (MOE curriculum alignment, AL1/PSLE-band language) that would look out of place on any other subject page. Strong support for these remaining fully separate, region-specific hub pages.

curriculum_family_findings.family: UK Entrance / Umbrella curricula (11+ Maths, 11+ English, British Curriculum, American Curriculum)
curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: 11+ Maths returns a UK-grammar-school-entrance-specific ecosystem (GoStudent, 11plustutoring.uk, Varsity Tutors eleven-plus-maths, Owl Tutors, Keystone 11-plus) with partial domain overlap against the GCSE family (Keystone, GoStudent recur as general UK multi-level platforms) but always via dedicated subpages -- differentiated. British Curriculum and American Curriculum (the catch-all umbrella subjects) surface YET ANOTHER distinct ecosystem of boutique expat-tutoring platforms (Private Tutors & Co, A+PlusOnlineTutoring, British Primary Tutor, Principal Tutors for British; A Plus Home Tutors, Tutero, APLUS America, PDO Tuition Services for American) targeting overseas/expat families specifically -- zero overlap between British and American ecosystems, and zero overlap with GCSE/AP specific pages. Confirms both umbrella subjects are legitimate standalone products (expat-market intent), not redundant with the curriculum-specific pages.

curriculum_family_findings.family: General academic subjects (Algebra I, Geometry, Calculus, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Middle School Math -- validated sample)
curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: CONFIRMED a consistent, THIRD distinct provider ecosystem: Tutor.com, Princeton Review, UPchieve, Wyzant, Superprof, Mathnasium, Varsity Tutors -- the general 'homework help' tutoring-marketplace pattern, clearly differentiated from both the exam-specific ecosystem (AP/GCSE/A-Level dedicated providers) and from each other (each subject gets its own dedicated subpage, e.g. tutor.com/subjects/physics vs /chemistry vs /biology vs /calculus vs /geometry, zero exact-URL overlap). This validates each general subject deserving its own hub page on a shared 'general academic tutor' template.
sibling_differentiation: Middle School Math (validated) is clearly its own SERP cluster (Mathnasium/middle-school, Varsity Tutors middle_school_math, Outschool, Brighterly, Princeton Review middle-grades-math) -- fully grade-specific subpages, zero overlap with Algebra I/Geometry generic results.

UNRESOLVED / MEDIUM CONFIDENCE: the American-curriculum 'Basics' cluster (Physics Basics, Chemistry Basics, Biology Basics, General Mathematics, Pre-Algebra, Middle School Math, Geometry Basics, General Science -- all Grades 6-8) was only spot-checked via Middle School Math, not pairwise against each other. Given how consistently every OTHER family in this research showed provider-level dedicated-subpage differentiation, the pattern likely extends, but this is a genuine research gap flagged for a follow-up pass before finalizing content for the other 7 'Basics' subjects.

FLAGGED RISK (pattern-inferred, not directly searched): 'algebra' (generic, curriculum=International, gradeLevel=All Levels) is a vague, ungraded duplicate of algebra-i / algebra-ii / pre-algebra / advanced-algebra with no differentiating modifier of its own -- same anachronistic-generic-sibling pattern found for ap-physics and ap-calculus above. Recommend either a clear differentiating content angle (an 'Algebra I vs II vs Pre-Algebra: which do I need?' chooser) or auditing whether this entry is redundant.

FLAGGED RISK (pattern-inferred, not directly searched): 'science' (generic, curriculum=International, All Levels) is a similarly vague duplicate of general-science (American, Grades 6-8) and gcse-science -- same generic-vs-specific risk pattern.

curriculum_family_findings.family: English-language-skills cluster (English, Academic English, Academic Writing, Essay Writing, Creative Writing, Grammar, Vocabulary, Reading Comprehension, Literature, Spoken English, GCSE English, SAT English, Cambridge English, IELTS -- 14 subjects touching 'English')
curriculum_family_findings.page_type_finding: LARGEST UNRESOLVED CLUSTER IN THIS RESEARCH. Only Essay Writing and Spoken English were directly validated (both show legitimate dedicated-subpage differentiation: Essay Writing on Tutor.com/HeyTutor/Princeton Review/Wyzant's own /essay-writing subpages; Spoken English on the conversational-practice ecosystem). The remaining 8 general-English subjects (English, Academic English, Academic Writing, Creative Writing, Grammar, Vocabulary, Reading Comprehension, Literature) were NOT individually searched this session. Given this is the single largest same-domain subject cluster in the entire 103-subject catalog, it is the highest-priority candidate for a dedicated full-depth follow-up SERP pass (Step 3b) before content is finalized for these 8 pages -- the validated members suggest the pattern of dedicated-subpage differentiation likely holds, but this should not be assumed without verification given the cluster's size and the real risk of several of these (e.g. 'Grammar' vs 'Vocabulary' vs generic 'English') collapsing into the same SERP.
